_comment_path: The interpreter path uses BACKSLASHES. cmd.exe parses a leading .venv/Scripts/... as the command `.venv` with a /Scripts switch, so the forward-slash form declared on 2026-08-15 exited in 0s with `'.venv' is not recognized` and the gate never ran once from the hook.
_comment_budget: The harness clamps timeoutSec to 170s, and above that it kills the hook and NO report is produced, which looks identical to a gate that was never declared. So the hook gate has to be bounded by something that does not grow with the dependency tree. It now runs `gates.py static`: ruff, import contracts, lizard. None of the three imports app code.
_comment_headroom: MEASURED 2026-08-18: static 8.4s cold, 3.2s warm (ruff 1.8s, import contracts 1.4s, lizard the rest). Against the 170s clamp that is 20x headroom, and it cannot erode by adding a dependency, because nothing here imports one. WHAT THIS REPLACED, and why: the gate was whole-suite --collect-only, measured 78.8s idle on 2026-08-15 with a warning in this very file that a heavy dependency would push it past the clamp. It did. On 2026-08-18 the same command took 142.5s standalone and was KILLED at 170s from the hook, reporting nothing at all. Collection cost is import cost (docling pulls transformers and torch), so it tracked the dependency tree rather than the suite, and no amount of test-writing discipline would have held it.
_comment_what_moved: Collection did not disappear, it moved. `gates.py fast` is static plus whole-suite collection; `gates.py full` is that plus the unit suite. Both are run deliberately and DETACHED (Start-Process -RedirectStandardOutput), never from the hook. The unit suite was 735.5s over 2376 tests on 2026-08-18.
full: cd apps/api && .venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\gates.py full && cd ../admin && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run check:no-dusk-tokens && npm run check:ops-room-wiring && npm run test:unit && cd ../widget && npm run build && node scripts/check-size.mjs
